units.spine: Goods for the market come in by the road. None of them are turned around here for sale somewhere else.
Spitzplatz is run in the open: its offices keep rooms, and every room answers to somebody.
People here can afford to argue about matters other than money.
Nothing about the town looks like it is waiting to fail. It earns its own keep.
The town's defences are kept sound, not kept for show.
Nobody in the town expects to lose a straight fight, and it bargains harder with its neighbours for that confidence.
The charter hall keeps people paid for whatever comes out of the wild, and the town counts that as its standing answer.
The main streets keep good order. The side streets keep less.
Prices in the town hold steady, steadier than a town living sale to sale could manage.
The town keeps no craft of its own for magic. When it is needed, it comes from outside.
Bread prices are watched here. In a comfortable town nobody would bother.
Political influence is what stands to change hands here, and The Governing Council and The Order of the Watch each know it well enough to be careful with the other.
The road runs by the town, and the town stays mostly outside whatever moves along it.
What the town cannot grow, the road brings in. Nothing here would keep it fed without that road.
The place is a town by any plain measure, too large to pass for a village and too small to pass for a city.
One tie in the town carries more weight than the rest, and it shapes what the town does and does not do.
Everyone in the town is tied to everyone else for the ordinary reasons: work, family, and proximity.
